title: What do translators charge per hour and how to plan your freelance finances
metaTitle: What do translators charge per hour? Financial planning for Mac users
description: Understand what do translators charge per hour and learn how to manage the feast and famine cycle on your Mac with simple financial planning.

intro: Many translators ask what do translators charge per hour to benchmark their own rates against industry standards. Setting a fair hourly rate requires accounting for non-billable hours like invoicing and project management, which often go uncompensated.
tldr: Most translators fail to include administrative hours in their hourly rate calculation.
Income volatility is the primary cause of burnout in the translation profession.
Use data-driven tracking to move from subjective feelings to objective financial health.
Establish a dedicated emergency fund to survive zero-work months.
Leverage Mac apps to automate expense tracking and tax preparation.

blocks.text: When you look at what do translators charge per hour, you often find a wide range of figures. This variation exists because translation is not a standardized commodity. Your rate depends on your language pair, your specialization, and your experience level. Many translators start by looking at market averages but quickly realize those numbers do not account for their specific overhead.

The core issue is that you are not just a translator. You are also a business owner. You spend time on email, invoicing, and research. If you only bill for the words you translate, you are effectively working for free during those administrative hours. This is why many freelancers feel they are underpaid even when their per-word rate seems competitive.

The gig economy creates a feast and famine cycle. You might have three massive projects in one month and zero the next. This unpredictability makes it hard to plan for taxes or retirement. Without a clear view of your cash flow, you might accept low-paying work just to bridge the gap during a slow period.

Many translators rely on subjective feelings about their income. You might feel like you are doing well because you are busy. However, without tracking your net earnings per client, you might be losing money on your most demanding accounts. You need to shift from feeling to facts.

items: Track every hour spent on non-billable tasks to calculate your true hourly cost.
Build an emergency fund covering at least three months of living expenses.
Factor your administrative overhead into your base rate for every new client.
Use a dedicated spreadsheet to log project totals and payment dates.
Review your income every month to spot trends in client demand.

faq.question: How do I calculate my hourly rate?
faq.answer: Add your desired annual income to your annual business expenses. Divide this total by the number of billable hours you can realistically work in a year. Ensure you include time for marketing, invoicing, and professional development.

faq.question: Is it better to charge per word or per hour?
faq.answer: Per-word pricing is standard for translation, but you should always use an hourly rate to check if your per-word rate covers your time and overhead. If a project takes longer than expected, your hourly rate drops.
